title: Front Running Bot for a Mint NFT on the sales - additions and clarifications - (cut from broadcast)
description: In this video, I talk about some aspects of the work of my script - a bot that allows NFT to mint on the saille, sending outstanding transactions, the Ethereum Mempool monitor as I showed you in one of the previous videos and implementing Front Running: https://github.com/bedrosovayulia/ethereumpendingtransactionchecker

asr.full_text: You probably remember that last week I demonstrated my work on MSM to a user on my own channel. I was monitoring my crypto network and seeing any incoming transactions on a smart-contract. There you can watch video with a simple transaction, i.e. an NFT-sale contract. nfc smart contract in t i copi vali some kind of transaction that we received and, accordingly, we send it ourselves at the same address of the same contract only, of course, signed our key for it to be performed in the first place that person's person who really sent it and accordingly so that we could grab and buy this valuable nfc, which could not be enough for us if we bought just by clicking on the site and here the commentators gave me what i forgot to set up, what transaction we actually caught and I put it in, by the way, during the process, I would like to thank the contributor who took the instructions of this repository for my description. Actually, let's go back to our code, here I corrected this part, I got asked many questions why this hash was used, what kind of numbers and letters they are. This is only a selector for a signature function we want to subscribe to. It's the method we want to catch and intercept using its own script. The selector is considered as the hash H3 of this function but it only takes the 4 bytes from this hash. Well, if we find in the transaction our function's hash, This is very very complicated. So in these transactions only 0.04 bytes are shown. So in this transaction we find our hash of our mint function, then we copy the transaction and redirect. And how are we to quickly draw this hash for any function that we want to catch when we just read someone's smart contract. So i will take a smart contract for NFT I will take same smart contract which you want to use to transfer your NFT collection there is a site which was developed already from the very beginning there are 6 sites for investing in the NFT smart contract, in fact, the transaction to which you want to intercept. There is a site that the smart people have already invented for us, so to say, this bicycle that allows us to code a signature of any function that we want to code. What do we need for this? Well, if we simply have a code of this smart contract that we received on blockchain, we go to the remix and then we create a new contract here and compile what it is, but preferably in the same compiler version, which was used for this contract, well, the compiler version was used there it is not applied to our application. Now, select a file and copy it obi go insert it on this site on this site we press the pars and here we choose the function for which we want to encoding a signature and, actually, here we insert how many nfc we want to buy and get that signature fully in the transaction, which would be if we sent this contract which I have now taken to the mint transaction, then in this transaction we will see just these symbols. Well, if you look in my repository, then I just hard-coded these symbols here. соответственно, вот таким образом You probably seen the hardcoded symbols inside my repository. This is the main method you can use to use these transactions in front of your smart contract that sends you any transaction to this contract and receive it, as I have shown in some of our videos this week.

annotation.contextual_rationale: The video's own title, description, repository presentation, and linked document present a front-running bot as a concrete NFT-sale mechanism, with the description directing viewers to the associated code repository. The demonstrated flow involves monitoring pending contract activity, identifying a mint function, copying and signing a transaction, and attempting to place it first, while the walkthrough also shows wallet connection, contract withdrawal code, and encoded transaction data. The material is framed as a technical demonstration or clarification of prior work rather than proof of a completed transaction, victim loss, or successful asset acquisition, so those outcomes and the speaker's inner intent remain unestablished.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The speaker describes a script that catches and intercepts a mint-function transaction, copies and redirects it, then sends a signed transaction to the same contract so it is performed first in order to buy the NFT. This supports an explicit transaction-priority or market-manipulation mechanism presented to obtain an asset; the evidence does not establish that it succeeded.
